title: Audience presence requirements fail open: an unrecognised persona_require_presence value is silently dropped, and persona_max_age is never enforced
description:
Two ways a relying party can ask for a presence guarantee and silently not get it.

(1) Unknown presence level degrades to no requirement. persona-core/src/audience.rs:132-133:

    if let Some(val) = param.strip_prefix("persona_require_presence=") {
        require_presence = PresenceLevel::from_str(val).unwrap_or(PresenceLevel::None);

PresenceLevel::from_str (assurance.rs:307-318) returns Err for anything outside {none, session, software, hardware}, and unwrap_or throws that error away. Trigger: a relying party writes persona_require_presence=Hardware (capitalised), =biometric, =hw, or any typo. The requirement silently becomes None and service.rs:146 passes unconditionally -- the RP believes it demanded hardware presence and gets a token with none. audience.rs:193-198 encodes this as intended behaviour in a passing test (unknown_presence_level_defaults_to_none), so it will not be caught by the suite.

This is inconsistent with the sibling parameter three lines down: audience.rs:134-138 makes an unparseable persona_max_age a hard AudienceParseError. A malformed value is an error for one parameter and a silent downgrade for the other, and the silent one is the security-relevant one.

(2) persona_max_age is parsed and then ignored. AudienceExtensions::max_age_secs (audience.rs:96-97) is populated by the parser but never read anywhere in persona-grpc/src/service.rs -- fetch_jwtsvid consults only ext.require_presence (service.rs:146). SPEC-HIA.md:250 documents persona_max_age=300 as part of the requirement expression, and SPEC-HIA.md:486 builds the sudo/PAM use case on require_presence=hardware&max_age=60. Trigger: an RP requests persona_max_age=60. The daemon issues a token asserting attested_at = now (service.rs:169) with no reference to when presence was actually established, and the RP has no way to tell its freshness constraint was discarded.

What goes wrong overall: both are fail-open. An RP that asks for a stronger guarantee than the daemon can provide gets a token that looks satisfactory rather than an UNAUTHENTICATED it can act on -- the behaviour SPEC-HIA.md:253 specifies.

Fix direction: return AudienceParseError for an unrecognised presence level (matching max_age handling), and either enforce max_age_secs against a real attestation timestamp or reject requests that carry it until presence timestamps are tracked.
close_reason: Fixed in 56ca5e5. Presence is now the fold of every audience's requirement, and the persona_ namespace is closed so unknown requirements are refused rather than defaulted to None. The .47 bypass was demonstrated failing against the old code before the fix. Also closed the unprefixed require_presence spelling, which the specs themselves recommended and which gated nothing.
